identity.title: MomaGraph: State-Aware Unified Scene Graphs with Vision-Language Models for Embodied Task Planning

problem.claim: Enable household mobile manipulators to navigate and manipulate using compact, semantically rich, task-relevant scene representations.

gap.claim: Prior scene-graph approaches often separate spatial and functional relations, omit object states and temporal updates, and overlook task-relevant information; suitable data and rigorous evaluation were also largely missing.

contributions.claim: MomaGraph unifies spatial-functional relationships with part-level interactive elements for embodied agents.
MomaGraph-Scenes is presented as a large-scale dataset of richly annotated, task-driven household scene graphs, paired with MomaGraph-Bench, an evaluation suite covering six reasoning capabilities.
MomaGraph-R1 is a 7B vision-language model trained with reinforcement learning to predict task-oriented scene graphs and perform zero-shot planning under Graph-then-Plan.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish their work through a unified task-driven scene-graph representation, a claimed first large-scale dataset of richly annotated task-driven household scene graphs, and a six-capability evaluation suite.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report 71.6% benchmark accuracy, 11.4 percentage points above the best baseline, with state-of-the-art performance among open-source models.
The authors report generalization across public benchmarks and effective transfer to real-robot experiments.

narrative_sequence.summary: Household mobile manipulators require both navigation and manipulation, motivating a compact, semantically rich representation.
Existing scene graphs are described as fragmented, static, and insufficiently focused on current-task information; data and evaluation are also missing.
The work introduces MomaGraph-Scenes and MomaGraph-Bench to provide task-driven data and systematic evaluation across six reasoning capabilities.
Using this foundation, the authors develop MomaGraph-R1 for task-oriented graph prediction and zero-shot Graph-then-Plan task planning.
The authors report strong benchmark performance plus cross-benchmark generalization and real-robot transfer.

source_observation.claim: The abstract aligns a representation, purpose-built dataset, multi-capability benchmark, and downstream planner, then reports results tied to that benchmark and transfer settings.

lessons.interpretation: A coherent contribution chain can make the relationship between representation design, evaluation, and deployment claims easy to follow.
lessons.application: When presenting a systems paper, explicitly connect each artifact to the capability it enables and report evidence in the same task-oriented terms.
lessons.exception: This structure may be unsuitable when the work has one isolated result or when artifacts are not genuinely coupled.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the six benchmark capabilities, dataset scale or annotation process, baseline identities, statistical details, or real-robot task and transfer metrics.
The reported accuracy and transfer claims lack experimental conditions and uncertainty information in the supplied units.
